children: AI data centres are set to account for about 20 per cent of Infineon’s revenue as the semiconductor industry increasingly focuses on the power infrastructure needed to support the growing AI compute demand, the company’s CEO Jochen Hanebeck said on Thursday.

Delivering a keynote at Semicon India 2026, Hanebeck said the AI opportunity extends beyond GPUs, models and memory to the power-generation, transmission, storage and delivery systems needed to run increasingly power-intensive data centres.

Hanebeck said AI’s growth would create opportunities across the power semiconductor chain, from renewable-energy generation and battery storage to high-voltage DC systems and solid-state transformers. “The big opportunities are on the infrastructure side: solid-state circuit breakers, 800-volt DC architecture, solid-state transformers. There is no compute without power, and we take care of it from grid to core. The other big thing is physical AI, which is also an opportunity because it’s an adjacent market,” the CEO added.
The architecture of cars and robots will all be built up in a similar way — a central compute, some storage, and all about zonal control, local control, communication, and sensing.

Infineon sees humanoid robotics as a market requiring complete subsystem solutions, including advanced sensing capabilities. Hanebeck said Infineon was working with customers on tactile sensing and other technologies needed for dexterous robotic hands.

Recently, Infineon announced the acquisition of C2i Semiconductors, a Bengaluru-based technology company specialising in software-defined multiphase controllers and smart power stages for AI data centre applications. Hanebeck noted that the company developed technology to help control power flows, particularly under rapidly changing loads in data centres.
The CEO said he hoped to welcome C2i’s employees to Infineon’s Bengaluru office soon.

title: AI data centres expected to drive 20% of Infineon’s revenue
